blocks.text: Penicillin is a group of bactericidal, antibiotics derived from Penicillium fungi, used to treat various bacterial infections by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis. Alexander Fleming (1928), discover it, which is highly effective against gram-positive bacteria, including streptococcal and staphylococcal infections. Common side effects of penicillin antibiotics include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and skin rashes.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 23.1 gives penicillin's target as 'Cell membrane' and spells 'Flurinolones'. Penicillin blocks cell wall synthesis, as the book's text says, and the correct name is fluoroquinolones; the drawing above shows both.
Penicillin adopt following way to kill bacteria;

items: Targeting Bacteria: Penicillin target bacteria because animal cells lack the cell walls that are targeted by the drug.
Cell Wall Inhibition: It interrupt the cross-linking of peptidoglycan (murein) chains, stopping new cell wall synthesis of bacteria.
Lysing bacterial Cell: The bacterial cell wall can no longer maintain structural integrity and it may burst (lysis), after the attack of penicillin (kills rather than just inhibits growth).
Resistance Mechanisms: Some bacteria defend themselves by producing specific enzymes like beta-lactamases.
